licensing.name: Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection, electrician licensing
licensing.description: DCP licenses electricians as individuals; only licensed contractors may pull permits or sign contracts, and odd-numbered licenses (e.g., E-1, L-3) are contractor licenses while even-numbered ones (e.g., E-2, L-2) are journeyman licenses.

licensing.name: Electrical Work Examining Board (Connecticut DCP)
licensing.description: State occupational board under the Department of Consumer Protection that oversees electrical work licensing; listed on the DCP Occupational Boards page.

funding.name: Connecticut Debt-Free Community College (Mary Ann Handley Award)
funding.provides: Debt-Free Tuition at CT State Community College provides tuition funding through the Mary Ann Handley Award for eligible students.
funding.eligibility: Register for at least 6 credits and fill out the FAFSA; funding is limited and awarded first-come, first-served
funding.how_to_apply: Apply, register for classes (6+ credits), and fill out the FAFSA

funding.name: CT Finish Line Scholarship
funding.provides: The CT Finish Line Scholarship covers mandatory tuition and fees at a participating CSCU four-year institution after other grants and scholarships are applied.
funding.eligibility: Connecticut resident; enrolled in a degree-seeking program at a CSCU four-year institution at least part-time (6+ credits); must have participated in the Debt-Free Community College, PACT or Mary Ann Handley award program and maintained eligibility

funding.name: CSCU financial aid (grants and scholarships)
funding.provides: The CSCU financial aid page describes federal, state and institutional grants and scholarships available to students, with staff help to determine eligibility.

funding.name: Connecticut Student Loan Reimbursement Program (SLRP)
funding.provides: The Student Loan Reimbursement Program awards money to Connecticut residents burdened with student loan debt.
funding.eligibility: Connecticut residents who have lived in the state for at least five years in a row immediately before the application date

funding.name: Connecticut Minority Advancement Program (MAP) grants
funding.provides: The Minority Advancement Program offers competitive grants to colleges, universities and nonprofits to fund programs that increase the diversity of students who attend and graduate from Connecticut colleges.
